narrative_purpose: Show the actual failure mode: not a wing burnt away but a wing shrunk. One membrane puckered into ridges while the other stays smooth, and the whole animal tipping into a roll it cannot correct.
subject: A large winged flying creature seen from behind and slightly above, both wings spread. Its LEFT wing membrane is drawn up into a series of tight parallel ridges and puckers near the rear edge, the ridged area covering roughly a third of that wing and looking shrunken and taut, with one small low flame at the very rear margin and a thin wisp of pale smoke. Its RIGHT wing membrane is smooth, full and evenly stretched. The whole body is tilted, the ridged wing dropping lower than the smooth one, so the creature is banking hard toward its damaged side. A small Na'vi rider clings low to its back.
scene: High in the air over a dark grey ash plain far below, ashen indigo sky with layered haze, no other objects nearby.
camera: From behind and slightly above the flying creature, showing the full span of both wings and the tilt of the body clearly against the sky.
light: Dim overcast ambient light on the wings from above; a small warm orange glow at the burning rear margin of the ridged wing lighting only its immediate surroundings.
palette: Cool grey-indigo across the wings and sky, the membranes a muted grey-teal; one small ember-orange point at the burning margin.
style: Painterly naturalist anatomical plate of a creature in flight, observed and clinical rather than dramatic.
detail_level: High on both wing membranes so the difference between the ridged and smooth surfaces reads clearly; the ground far below flat and hazed.
composition: The creature centred with its wings spanning most of the width, the tilt obvious against the horizon, broad areas of plain dim sky above each wing kept clear and low-detail for overlaid callouts.
consistency_notes: CRITICAL: the wing is CONTRACTED, not consumed. The membrane must still be present and continuous — ridged, puckered and drawn up, with no large burnt holes and no sheet of flame. Only one small flame at the rear margin. The asymmetry between the two wings and the resulting body tilt are the whole point.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows or rotation indicators, no wing engulfed in flames, no large burnt holes, no explosion, no 3D-render or photographic look, no cartoon style
